A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same MUDG research. Despite the changed title and substantial expansion, methods, experiments, figures and appendix material can be matched reliably. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across 20 benchmarks, retrieval and clustering ablations, hyperparameter studies, and a Terra Incognita pseudo-labeling case study.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification, nearest-neighbor retrieval, adaptive augmentation and component-ablation results, alongside retained experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds paired k-means indexing, replaces random query augmentation with adaptive descriptor selection, and replaces plain cross-entropy finetuning with a diversity-preserving objective using initial predictions (Sections 3.1–3.3). Rank pseudo-labeling and clustering-based sample selection remain core components.

E1.justification: All 20 classification benchmarks and the LAION-2B source remain. v2 substantially extends task coverage to approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, including image-to-image, text-to-text and text-to-image evaluation, and adds a synthetic Gaussian retrieval scenario (Figures 2–4 and 8). Other source datasets mentioned in the introduction are not demonstrated experimentally.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CuPL for both backbones and author-reported SuS-X results for ViT-B/16, introducing a directly relevant MUDG comparator. New comparisons also include standard versus paired k-means, alternative training losses, and random sample selection. v1's GPT Descriptors is retained under the name Visual Descriptors.

E3.justification: v2 introduces retrieval protocols measuring R@1 against probe count and query latency at 4-, 8- and 16-bit quantization levels. It also documents a 20M-LAION analysis and a 10,000-point, 20-cluster Gaussian demonstration. Existing classification backbones, training budgets and dataset-specific retrieval settings remain largely unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds component ablations for indexing, adaptive augmentation and the training loss; alternative-loss and random-selection controls; convergence analyses; descriptor-quality examples; and probe-count sensitivity (Figures 3–5 and 10; Tables 4–6 and 11). Earlier hubness and sample-selection analyses largely survive in Appendix C, although the ViT-L/14 skip-clustering results are no longer reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification averages over three experiments or trials. Neither introduces experimental error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests or seed reporting; the expanded results do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many MUDG entries are replaced with results for the revised pipeline: ViT-B/16 ImageNet changes from 69.9 to 70.4, Aircraft from 33.7 to 32.8, and Terra Incognita mean from 37.2 to 38.7. The eleven-dataset mean remains 71.1. New retrieval, augmentation and ablation outcomes substantially expand the results, while PACS/VLCS scores are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds spherical and Gaussian assumptions, two theorems, a corollary, probability-density derivations, and proofs and geometric arguments in Appendix A. This is a substantial theoretical addition to v1's algorithmic formulation. Theorem 1 and its proof contain inconsistent definitions and interpretations of rho.

C1.justification: The main contribution shifts from introducing MUDG and a three-stage dataset-construction pipeline to explaining modality-gap retrieval failures and proposing improved indexing, adaptive augmentation and diversity-preserving finetuning. The abstract and contribution list additionally claim stronger retrieval and zero-shot performance and comparisons with name-only transfer methods.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations linking query–centroid distance to retrieval failures, label-feature variance to descriptor quality, and initial-prediction regularization to preserved diversity. It acknowledges restrictive theoretical assumptions and an unproved geometric implication. Existing hubness explanations and limitations concerning source coverage, semantic alignment and saturated zero-shot accuracy remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 9 add index and augmentation hyperparameters, descriptor-bank provenance, the loss weight, GPU resources, storage requirements, and timings for indexing, retrieval, labeling, clustering and downloading. v1 documented basic finetuning and dataset-specific settings but lacked this infrastructure and runtime information. The code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions MUDG alongside SuS-X's name-only transfer setting and develops a new relationship to modality-gap and retrieval-adaptation research. It adds citations supporting these connections, the adopted diversity-preserving loss, and the mathematical analysis. This substantially revises positioning beyond the earlier emphasis on data-centric dataset construction.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, gains an author, and extensively rewrites its abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion around cross-modal retrieval. Much of the original method exposition moves into Appendix C, while proofs become Appendix A and experimental details become Appendix B.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, combines the earlier pipeline diagrams with new components in Figure 1, and adds retrieval, theory, ablation and radar graphics. Results tables are reorganized, and many existing qualitative figures and domain results move to the appendices. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through SuS-X comparisons, component and loss ablations, retrieval diagnostics, and computational-cost documentation. However, its new headline theory has correctness concerns: Theorem 1 describes rho(s') as close to 1, while Appendix A.1 defines rho below 0.5 and equates that single-sample quantity with an n-sample nearest-neighbor probability. These inconsistencies undermine the theoretical contribution. The empirical and reproducibility gains are clear, but their net effect against these new reliability problems cannot be assessed confidently.
